newsitem.title: FINLAND: Wireless protocol gains momentum - Nokia.
newsitem.headline: Wireless protocol gains momentum - Nokia.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications equipment group Nokia said in a statement on Monday that industry support was growing for the wireless protocol developed by it, Ericsson, Motorola and Unwired Planet.

"Ericsson, Motorola, Nokia and Unwired Planet today announced growing industry support for the Wireless Application Protocol effort..., with Alcatel, Mitsubishi Electric, Nortel, Philips Consumer Communications and Siemens Private Communications Systems Group (PN) endorsing the initiative," Nokia said.
The initiative was announced on June 26, it said.
The draft protocol would be made available to cellular phone manufacturers and operators around the world and was expected to be published on the World Wide Web by September 15.

The protocol will be independent of the underlying airlink standard and initially target GSM (Global System for Mobile Communication) networks. The aim is to align industry efforts to bring advanced applications and Internet content to digital celllar phones, it said.
"For cellular phone manufacturers, a common standard means potential for realising economies of scale," Nokia said, adding this would encourage them to develop compatible hardware.

Nokia also said the industry group acknowledged support for the Handheld Device Markup Language (HDML) as submitted to the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) as the basis for the new Wireless Application Protocol microbrowser.
"The transport protocol will be based on the narroband sockets specification," it added.
